title: Ancestral origins of environmental (in)attention
abstract: arXiv:2509.09598v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: How do ancestral climate experiences shape today's attitudes towards environmental issues? Combining multiple contemporary surveys and ethnic group-level cultural records with a model of cultural selection on costly attention, we show that ancestral climate anomalies have a lasting U-shaped effect on environmental concern. Descendants of groups exposed to the most regular and the most anomalous climates attach greater importance to the environment, with a dip in between; a pattern mirrored in cultural narratives. But why should contemporary environmental concern remain anchored in ancestral climates when lessons about the value of environmental attention can be learned beyond the conditions in which they were initially acquired? Our model shows that because attention is chosen before conditions are realized, cultural selection rewards perceptions that perform well on average without fully correcting their accuracy across conditions.

translated_title: 环境关注与否的祖先起源
translated_abstract: 祖先的气候经历如何塑造当今人们对环境问题的态度？我们将多项当代调查、族群层面的文化记录与一个关于代价性注意的文化选择模型相结合，结果表明祖先经历的气候异常对环境关注具有持久的U型影响。生活在最规律气候和最异常气候中的族群，其后代更重视环境，而中间地带则出现低谷；这一模式在文化叙事中同样有所体现。然而，既然关于环境关注价值的经验教训可以在其最初习得的条件之外继续学习，为什么当代的环境关注仍然锚定于祖先的气候？我们的模型表明，由于注意是在条件实现之前做出选择的，文化选择会奖励那些在平均意义上表现良好、却未能在不同条件下完全校正其准确性的认知。
tldr: 该研究结合调查数据与文化选择模型发现，祖先经历的气候异常对后代的环境关注产生持久的U型影响——气候最规律与最异常族群的后代更重视环境，其根源在于注意在条件实现前即被选择，文化选择只奖励平均表现良好而未按条件校正准确性的认知。
en_tdlr: Combining surveys, ethnic-group cultural records, and a cultural selection model, this study finds that ancestral climate anomalies leave a lasting U-shaped effect on environmental concern, because attention is chosen before conditions are realized, so cultural selection rewards perceptions that perform well on average without fully correcting their accuracy across conditions.
